name: Myeongdong Kyoja (명동교자 본점)
notes: Hand-cut noodle house. Michelin dates it to 1966; VisitKorea says 1970 — the two official sources conflict, so treat the founding year as uncertain. Not a Bib Gourmand.

name: Imun Seolnongtang (이문설농탕)
notes: The first restaurant officially registered in Seoul (1907). Beef leg bone simmered 17 hours into a clean, milky broth; suyuk and suyuk muchim are also specialties. Not a Bib Gourmand.

name: Hadongkwan (하동관 본점)
notes: Established 1939. Clean but deeply savoury gomtang with brisket, offal and tripe, rice warmed in the broth, Seoul-style kkakdugi. Opens early and closes when the soup vats run dry — go early. Not a Bib Gourmand.
hours: Mon–Sat 07:00–16:00 (or until sold out). Closed Sun.

name: Chanyang-jip (찬양집)
notes: Kalguksu with clams. VisitKorea dates it to the early 1970s. This guide previously claimed a Bib Gourmand — that was wrong. Michelin lists only two Bib Gourmand kalguksu restaurants in Seoul (Hwangsaengga and Limbyungjoo Sandong), and this is not one of them.

name: Hwangsaengga Kalguksu (황생가칼국수)
notes: Beef-bone kalguksu, wang mandu, hanu suyuk. VisitKorea also records a 2023 Michelin listing. Michelin: long queues; open all day. ☎ +82-2-739-6334

name: Sinseonggak (신성각)
notes: Old-school Korean-Chinese jajangmyeon. Lunch only, and it closes as soon as it sells out.
hours: 11:35–15:00, until sold out. Closed Sun, New Year's Day, and the Seollal & Chuseok holidays.

name: Ohsaegyehyang (오세계향)
notes: Vegan Korean-Chinese, including vegan jajangmyeon. Note the mid-afternoon break and the Thursday closure.

name: Pildong Myeonok (필동면옥)
notes: Pyeongyang-style mul naengmyeon; Visit Seoul: eat with Pyeongan-style mandu or jeyuk. Address matches MICHELIN. Visit Seoul last edited 4 Jun 2026. ☎ +82-2-2266-2611

name: Sadong Myeonok (사동면옥)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 9 Jun 2026): Hwanghae-style boiled fist-sized mandu; also doganitang, nokdujeon, pajeon. ☎ +82-2-725-1211

name: Insadong Sujebi (인사동수제비)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 4 Jun 2026): sujebi in earthenware; spicy oyster sujebi; haemul pajeon. ☎ +82-2-735-3361
hours: Weekdays 11:30–14:50 / 17:00–20:40. Weekends & holidays 11:30–15:20 / 17:00–20:40. Closed public holidays.

name: Myeongdong Hamheung Myeonok (명동함흥면옥)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 29 Jul 2026): Hamgyong-style hoe naengmyeon; opened in Myeongdong in the late 1970s; first-generation owners from Hwanghae. ☎ +82-2-776-8430

name: Nampo Myeonok (남포면옥)
michelin: VisitKorea: Michelin listings “several times.” Not treated as 2026 Bib here.
notes: VisitKorea: opened 1968; Pyeongyang naengmyeon; also galbitang, bulgogi, mandu soup, yukgaejang. ☎ +82-2-777-3131
hours: Weekdays 11:30–22:00 / weekends 11:30–21:00. Closed Seollal day & Chuseok day.

name: Hyundai Kalguksu (현대칼국수)
notes: VisitKorea: two generations since 1982; anchovy–pollack–kelp broth; extra rice/noodles free per the listing. ☎ +82-2-752-9504
hours: 09:00–21:00 / Sat 09:00–19:00. Closed Sundays and national holidays.

name: Halmeoni Kalguksu (할머니칼국수)
notes: VisitKorea: noodle soup and dumpling soup. Same lane cluster as Chanyang-jip. ☎ +82-2-744-9548

name: Geumdwaeji Sikdang (금돼지식당)
notes: Bone-in pork samgyeopsal. One of only two Bib Gourmand barbecue restaurants in Seoul. Expect a long wait; take a number in person.

name: Budnamujip (버드나무집)
notes: Open since 1977. Beef only — this is not a pork restaurant, and it is not in Mapo. An earlier draft of this guide listed it as "Budnamujip Mapo" serving pork ribs; that entry was wrong on location, meat and hours.

name: Chung Ki Wa Town Main Branch (청기와타운 본점)
nameEn: Chung Ki Wa Town Main Branch
notes: VisitKorea: Korean barbecue; Suwon jumbo grilled galbi (from 2 servings) and LA galbi; aged meat on display; tojang jjigae. Not Myeongdong — Yeongdeungpo. ☎ +82-507-1316-1474

name: Janganmun (장안문)
notes: VisitKorea: grilled beef brisket; also jumbo beef ribs and spareribs. Near Euljiro 1-ga. ☎ +82-2-755-0673

name: Buchon Yukhoe (부촌육회)
michelin: VisitKorea: 2020 MICHELIN Guide listing. Not in the 2026 Seoul Bib Gourmand (51). Current global MICHELIN page: Restaurant not found.
notes: VisitKorea describes a three-generation restaurant. House dish: beef tartare; also sliced raw beef. Take-out available. ☎ +82-2-2267-1831 · bcyukhoe.modoo.at (Korean only). A 2025 Bib Gourmand label is not independently confirmed on the current MICHELIN site and is not used here.

name: Jin Ok-hwa Halmae Wonjo Dakhanmari (진옥화할매원조닭한마리)
notes: Founded 1978. Whole chicken soup (dakhanmari); toppings include noodles. Address is Jongno-gu, not Jung-gu.

name: Goryeo Samgyetang (고려삼계탕 본점)
notes: Ginseng chicken soup. VisitKorea records a 2023 Michelin listing; it is not in the current Bib Gourmand selection. The "first samgyetang restaurant in Korea, since 1960" claim in earlier drafts could not be confirmed by any official source and has been removed.
hours: Daily 10:30–21:00. Closed for the Seollal & Chuseok holidays.

name: Myeongdongjeong (명동정)
notes: Korean table d'hôte (hanjeongsik). VisitKorea: myeongdong jeongsik (bulgogi set), weekday lunch youngran sang, gwibin sang. Break mid-afternoon. ☎ +82-2-3789-5130

name: Myeongdong Eomeonijip (명동어머니집)
notes: Haemultang / spicy baby-octopus hot pot. Visit Seoul last edited 13 Nov 2024. ☎ +82-2-776-3896

name: Yeongyang Center (영양센터)
notes: Korean-style rotisserie whole chicken. Visit Seoul last edited 5 Jun 2026. ☎ +82-2-776-2015

name: Myeongdong Chungmu Gimbap (명동충무김밥)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 30 Jun 2026): one dish — Chungmu gimbap set (gimbap, spicy squid, pickled radish); over 40 years in Myeongdong. No alcohol. ☎ +82-2-755-8488

name: Yennal Myeongdong Budaejjigae (옛날명동부대찌개)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 8 Jun 2026): budae jjigae with pork, ham, sausage; also samgyeopsal. ☎ +82-2-752-6800

name: Wonjo Namsan Wangdonkkaseu Myeongdong (원조남산왕돈까스 명동)
notes: VisitKorea: jumbo pork cutlet / cheese pork cutlet. Holiday field says “Open 24/7” while hours are 11:00–22:00 — treat as open all year, not 24-hour. ☎ +82-2-319-0120

name: Yukdaejang Myeongdong (육대장 명동)
notes: VisitKorea listing for this Myeongdong address (Yukdaejang is a national chain — these hours are only for this page). Spicy beef soup (yukgaejang). ☎ +82-2-775-7555

name: Myeongdong Hanubang (명동한우방)
notes: VisitKorea: grilled thin skirt (Hanu BBQ). ☎ +82-2-2267-8132

name: Seowon (서원)
notes: VisitKorea: porridge house (abalone, chicken, shrimp juk); opens early. ☎ +82-2-776-0214 · seowonjuk.modoo.at
hours: Mon–Sat 07:00–17:00 / Sun 07:00–14:00. Closed every other Wednesday.

name: Nwijo (뉘조)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 4 Jun 2026): medicinal / wild-vegetable kitchen (geunchaessam, bburi beombeok). ☎ +82-507-1497-9303

name: Hanaro Hwaegwan (하나로회관)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 28 Apr 2026): traditional Korean kitchen; listing says 28 years in Insadong. Mid-afternoon break. ☎ +82-2-732-7451

name: Sanchon (산촌)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 5 May 2026): temple food by a former monk; vegetable/mountain-herb table, no meat. ☎ +82-2-735-0312 · sanchon.com

name: Hamcho Ganjang Gejang (함초간장게장)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 15 Jun 2026): soy-sauce marinated crab (ganjang-gejang) in fermented herb soy sauce; menus in EN/JP/CN. ☎ +82-2-318-1624 · hamchogejang.com

name: Jeonju Hoegwan (전주회관)
notes: VisitKorea: more than 50 years; patented gopdol bibimbap; also yukhoe bibimbap, Jeonju kongnamul gukbap, galbitang, samgyetang. ☎ +82-2-778-6689 · jeonju6689.co.kr

name: Jungsungbon Shabu Suki Kalguksu (정성본샤브수끼칼국수)
notes: VisitKorea: shabu-shabu and yukhoe. Holiday field “Open 24/7” while hours are 10:30–22:00 — treat as open all year. ☎ +82-2-752-4800

name: Janggeumi Jeonjip (장금이전집)
notes: VisitKorea: stir-fried seafood and mung-bean pancake. Holiday field “Open 24/7” while hours run 11:30–02:00 — treat as open all year, not 24-hour. ☎ +82-2-771-5279

name: Yonggeumok (용금옥)
notes: VisitKorea: established 1932; Seoul-style chutang (whole loach, not ground Namwon style); also pan-fried loach and grilled dried pollack. ☎ +82-2-777-1689
hours: 11:00–22:00. Closed the 2nd, 4th, and 5th Sunday of each month.

name: Geumseonggwan Najugomtang (금성관나주곰탕)
notes: VisitKorea: Naju-style gomtang and galbitang. ☎ +82-2-753-7898

name: Sikdang Jin (식당진)
notes: VisitKorea: Japanese home-style; katsudon and sake don. Near Myeongdong Station. ☎ +82-2-755-7558

name: Minsokchon (민속촌)
notes: VisitKorea: grilled strip loin and grilled beef ribs. Hours 00:00–24:00 and holiday “Open 24/7” — treat as open 24 hours, year-round. ☎ +82-2-779-8371

name: Jongno Myeongtaedeokjang (종로명태덕장)
notes: VisitKorea: braised pollack and ray hot pot. Holiday field “Open 24/7” while hours are 10:30–22:30 — treat as open all year. ☎ +82-2-771-9201

name: Nakji Wangguk (낙지왕국)
notes: VisitKorea: stir-fried octopus and octopus soup. ☎ +82-2-765-3119

name: Gobong Samgyetang (고봉삼계탕)
notes: VisitKorea: samgyetang with Korean herbs; also dakjuk and jjimdak. Same building number as Wonjo Namsan Wangdonkkaseu (that shop is 1F). ☎ +82-2-756-2300

name: Jeongwon Sutbulgalbi (정원숯불갈비)
notes: VisitKorea: marinated grilled beef ribs and boneless short rib. ☎ +82-2-765-1305

name: Dongdaemun Bonga Gamasot Seolleongtang (동대문본가가마솥설렁탕)
notes: VisitKorea: seolleongtang boiled 24 hours in a cast-iron pot (visible from outside); also yennal bulgogi and yukhoe bibimbap. Near Dongdaemun Fashion Market. ☎ +82-2-741-1510

name: Neungnabapsang (능라밥상)
notes: VisitKorea: North Korean kitchen (chef described as a defector); boiled meat platter and soy-sauce bibimbap. Holiday field “Open 24/7” while hours are 11:00–21:00 — treat as open all year. ☎ +82-2-733-9905

name: RADOST (라도스트)
notes: VisitKorea: deep-fried then braised boneless chicken; also barbecue. Holiday field “Open 24/7” while hours are 14:00–01:00 — treat as open all year. ☎ +82-2-734-8945

name: THE SIC-DDANG Myeongdong (더식당 명동)
notes: VisitKorea: Korean and Western; lobster and cockle salad listed. Holiday field “Open 24/7” while hours are 11:00–23:00 — treat as open all year. ☎ +82-2-318-2234

name: Okcheon Maeun Jokbal (옥천매운족발)
notes: VisitKorea: spicy braised jokbal; herbal jokbal also listed. Near Dongdaemun. ☎ +82-2-3672-7168

name: Masan Place (마산집)
notes: VisitKorea: over 40 years; soegogi gukbap and modeum jeon. Closed weekends. ☎ +82-2-752-2415

name: Namhae Gulgukbap (남해굴국밥)
notes: VisitKorea: oyster gukbap; oysters listed as from Tongyeong daily; also raw oyster salad. ☎ +82-2-764-4858

name: Hongsugye Jjimdak (홍수계찜닭)
notes: VisitKorea: soy-sauce jjimdak. Mall floor — confirm the shop is still on 5F. ☎ +82-2-772-9389

name: Heukdonga Myeongdong (흑돈가 명동)
notes: VisitKorea listing for this Myeongdong basement (Heukdonga is a chain). Jeju black-pork ogyeopsal on charcoal. Same building as Gobong (2F) and Namsan donkkaseu (1F). ☎ +82-2-3789-0080

name: Jinju Hoegwan (진주회관)
notes: VisitKorea: kongguksu March–November; also kimchi bokkeumbap and samgyeopsal. Page prints weekday close as “11:00-21”. ☎ +82-2-753-5388

name: Yennal Yeongil Naengmyeon (옛날연길냉면)
notes: VisitKorea: cold buckwheat noodles and boiled dumplings; listing says run by a Chinese owner. ☎ +82-2-747-8898

name: Jaembaeok (잼배옥)
notes: VisitKorea: “over 80 years”; seolleongtang and hangover soup. Saturday lunch only. ☎ +82-2-755-8106
hours: Weekdays 10:00–21:10 (break 15:00–17:00) / Sat 11:00–15:00. Closed Sundays and national holidays.

name: Gangseo Myeonok (강서면옥)
notes: VisitKorea: Pyeongyang-style naengmyeon over fifty years; Gangwon buckwheat; also mandu jeongol. ☎ +82-2-752-1945

name: Mirakjeong (미락정)
notes: VisitKorea: house-made jumbo pork cutlet from domestic pork. ☎ +82-2-778-7210

name: Miseongok (미성옥)
notes: VisitKorea: ox-bone soup and suyuk; listing dates the shop to 1966. Holiday field says “Open 24/7” while hours are 06:00–22:00 — treat as open all year. ☎ +82-2-776-8929

name: Myth Jokbal Myeongdong (미쓰족발명동)
notes: VisitKorea: jokbal and bossam; garlic jokbal listed as main. ☎ +82-2-3789-8799

name: Myeongdong Seoseo Galbi (명동서서갈비)
notes: VisitKorea: grilled beef ribs; no seating — standing only. ☎ +82-2-318-6400

name: Jangsu Galbi (장수갈비)
notes: VisitKorea: grilled ribs and bulgogi; listing dates the shop to 1968. ☎ +82-2-775-9292

name: Jongno Samgyetang (종로삼계탕)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 30 Jun 2026): two-generation samgyetang; abalone, herbal, perilla-seed versions. Alcohol sold. ☎ +82-507-1322-8761
hours: Mon–Fri 11:00–21:00 (break 15:00–17:00, last order 20:15). Sat 11:00–15:00 (last order 14:15). Closed Sundays.

name: Gyeongin Misulgwan Jeontong Dawon (경인미술관 전통다원)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 5 May 2026): traditional tea and snacks in a restored hanok garden at Kyungin Museum of Fine Art. ☎ +82-507-1339-6305
hours: Daily 11:00–21:20. Closed New Year’s Day, Seollal & Chuseok.

name: Gukje Milmyeon Main Branch (국제밀면 본점)
notes: Busan's signature cold wheat noodle dish, in both mul (broth) and bibim (spicy mixed) form. ☎ 051-501-5507

name: Halmae Gaya Milmyeon (할매가야밀면)
notes: Milmyeon and bibim milmyeon. Visit Busan credits it with about 40 years of history and notes a 140-seat room, so the queue at mealtimes moves faster than it looks. The "founded 1974" claim in earlier drafts is not supported by the official listing. ☎ 051-246-3314

name: Seo-myeon Gaegeum Milmyeon (서면개금밀면)
notes: Milmyeon in a herbal beef-bone broth. Takeout available. The "since 1966" claim in earlier drafts could not be confirmed and has been removed. ☎ +82-51-802-0456

name: Gijang Sonkalguksu (기장손칼국수)
notes: Hand-rolled knife-cut noodles, served with gimbap. The "Baek Jong-won's Top 3 Chefs" claim in earlier drafts has no official source and has been removed. ☎ +82-51-806-6832 **Corroborated and refined 19 Aug 2026:** the Blue Ribbon index lists it as "Gijangson kalguksu" at the same address with the same 09:00–21:00 hours, and adds that it closes on Lunar New Year's Day and Chuseok — days the listing used here does not mention.

name: Dongnae Milmyeon (동래밀면)
notes: Visit Busan: milmyeon house of nearly 30 years; also deulkkae kalguksu, marsh-snail soup, jumbo dumplings. (The BTS/RM celebrity framing is on the official page; it is not independently checked here.) Parking noted by Visit Busan.

name: Daeyeon Milmyeon (대연밀면)
notes: Visit Busan: opened 2011; bibim milmyeon and deulkkae kalguksu. Short day — last order 16:50. ☎ +82-507-1355-6120

name: Samseong Milmyeon (삼성밀면)
notes: Visit Busan: milmyeon specialist; page says 60 years and first-generation owner still running. ☎ 051-806-1256

name: Gaya Halmae Milmyeon (가야할매밀면)
notes: Different restaurant from Halmae Gaya Milmyeon in Nampo. Visit Busan: cornstarch-elastic noodles; pork-and-beef-bone broth. ☎ +82-51-865-8017

name: Ilmi Milmyeon (일미밀면)
notes: Visit Busan: ox-bone milmyeon; also dwaeji gukbap (not in summer, per the official page). ☎ +82-51-463-3977 · ilmimilmyeon.modoo.at. The page also prints a closure Mon 19 May–Sun 1 Jun with no year — treat that as a dated notice, not a recurring rule.

name: Yangpyeong Kalguksu (양평칼국수)
notes: Visit Busan: owner-made ripened kalguksu dough; kimchi from domestic napa; summer-only cold noodles. Far from Nampo/Seomyeon — plan a ride to Dadaepo. ☎ +82-51-265-0907
hours: Mon–Fri 11:00–20:00 (break 15:30–17:00, last order 19:30). Sat 11:00–15:30 (last order 15:00). Closed Sundays.

name: Danggam Milmyeon (당감밀면)
address: 5 Danggam-ro, Samik Apt. arcade B-dong 1F, Busanjin-gu
notes: Visit Busan (Korean listing): milmyeon, bibim milmyeon, handmade mandu, son kalguksu. ☎ 051-896-0177

name: Hwaguk Banjeom (화국반점)
notes: Korean-Chinese kitchen that Visit Busan credits with 43 years of history; known for ganjjajang and tangsuyuk, and used as a filming location for New World and Nameless Gangster. Note the mid-afternoon break — earlier drafts listed it as open straight through. ☎ 051-245-5305
hours: 11:30–15:30 / 17:00–21:30. Closed the 1st & 3rd Monday of each month.

name: Banpin (반핀)
notes: Visit Busan: casual Taiwanese; char siu rice bowl and mapo tofu; binchotan toppings. Companion animals allowed per the listing. Not Korean cuisine. ☎ +82-507-1498-6223
hours: Weekdays 11:30–16:00 / 17:00–21:00. Weekends 11:15–16:00 / 17:00–21:00. (Page prints last order 15:00 — that sits inside the lunch window; confirm last order on the day.) Open all year.

name: Haeundae Amso Galbijip (해운대암소갈비집)
notes: Opened 1964. Hanu saenggalbi grilled on the house's own iron pan, with gamja guksu (potato noodles) to finish. Earlier drafts called this "Haeundae Somunnan Amso Galbi-jip" — that name is wrong. Closed for Seollal and Chuseok. ☎ +82-51-746-0033 · haeundaegalbi.com

name: Geodae Galbi (거대갈비)
notes: Visit Busan: charcoal Hanu barbecue; listing notes high prices. ☎ 051-746-0037 **Corroborated 19 Aug 2026:** Visit Busan's Blue Ribbon "100 Great Places to Eat in Busan" index lists the same restaurant as "Geodae sutbulgui" at the same address with the same hours (11:30–15:00 / 17:00–22:00, open all year). Two official sources agree.

name: 88 Dwaeji Galbi (88돼지갈비)
notes: Visit Busan: marinaded pork barbecue; listing says 40 years. ☎ 051-468-3065

name: Busan Jokbal (부산족발)
address: 13 Gwangbok-ro, Jung-gu (Jokbal Alley, near Gukje Market)
notes: Naengchae jokbal — cold pig's trotter with jellyfish and mustard sauce. The "original 50-year inventor" claim in earlier drafts is unsourced and has been removed. Open all year. ☎ +82-507-1412-5359

name: Songjeong Samdae Gukbap (송정3대국밥)
notes: Dwaeji gukbap (pork and rice soup) and suyuk baekban — Busan's defining comfort dish. Open year-round; no on-site parking. The "operating since 1946" claim in earlier drafts is unsourced and has been removed. ☎ +82-507-1412-5722

name: Jamae Gukbap (자매국밥)
notes: Visit Busan: pork-head broth, doenjang seasoning; over 30 years. ☎ 051-752-1912

name: Jaegi Dwaeji Gukbap (재기돼지국밥)
notes: Visit Busan: toryeom-style dwaeji gukbap; listing says 55 years. Closes when sold out. ☎ +82-51-418-0526
hours: 08:00–21:00 or until sold out. Closed Mondays.

name: Ungcheonjip (웅천집)
address: 7-14 Geumgok-daero 616beon-gil (Visit Busan does not print the district on this page)
notes: Visit Busan: three generations since 1964; leather carp hoe, catfish maeuntang, grilled eel; soy sauce aged three years. ☎ +82-51-332-8740
hours: Daily 11:30–21:30. Break 15:00–16:00. Last order 20:30. Open 365 days.

name: Samihun (사미헌)
notes: Visit Busan: Hanwoo specialist; galbitang and myeongjang set; private rooms. ☎ 051-819-6677

name: Yeongjin Sikdang (영진식당)
notes: Visit Busan (Korean listing): dwaeji gukbap and suyuk baekban. Same address as the “Yeongjin Dwaeji Gukbap main” listing. Portal prices are not copied. ☎ 051-206-3820

name: Cor Pasta Bar (코르 파스타바)
notes: Visit Busan: handmade pasta and bread; bar-like room. On the official 2026 Busan Bib list (Italian). Portal prices are not copied. ☎ +82-507-1474-4570

name: Dongnae Halmae Pajeon (동래할매파전)
notes: Four generations of Dongnae-style pajeon — whole spring onions with seafood, bound in a rice-flour batter. Earlier drafts listed the hours and closing day incorrectly (they said Wed–Sun 12:00–22:00, closed Mon & Tue). ☎ 051-552-0792

name: Jagalchi Market (자갈치시장)
notes: Korea's largest seafood market. Buy fresh fish on the ground floor and have it prepared upstairs. Individual stalls set their own hours within the market's window. ☎ +82-51-245-2594
hours: 05:00–22:00. Closed the 1st & 3rd Tuesday of each month.

name: Bujeon Market (부전시장)
notes: Busan's largest traditional market, liveliest early in the morning when produce and seafood are traded direct. Hours differ by shop — the figure below is the market-wide window, and earlier drafts listed it wrongly as 09:00–18:00. ☎ +82-51-818-7009

name: Samjin Eomuk Main Store (삼진어묵 본점)
notes: Korea's best-known fish-cake brand, run by the same family since 1953 (three generations) — this is the original Yeongdo store. There is a fish-cake making workshop on the 2nd floor. Parking available. ☎ 051-715-5865 · samjinfood.com

name: Brown Hands Baekje (브라운핸즈 백제)
notes: A cafe inside Busan's first modern Western-style hospital building, a registered cultural property; the interior deliberately preserves the age of the structure. Espresso and americano are the house drinks. The "1922" build date in earlier drafts is not in the official listing. ☎ 051-464-0332

name: Choryang Ondang (초량온당)
notes: Visit Busan: bakery; queues at opening; yellow-cheese bread is the listed favorite. Portal menu prices are not copied here. ☎ +82-507-1318-1271

name: Nampo Samgyetang (남포삼계탕)
notes: Visit Busan: more than 50 years; samgyetang with glutinous rice, ginseng, chestnut, jujube; electric grilled chicken also listed. Portal prices are not copied. ☎ +82-51-245-5075
hours: Mon–Fri 11:00–20:50 (break 15:30–16:30, last order 20:20). Sat–Sun 11:00–20:50 (last order 20:20). Closed traditional holidays.

name: Bonsuwon Galbi (본수원갈비)
notes: VisitKorea: over 50 years; saeng-galbi and yangnyeom-galbi; wanggalbi is the listed main dish. Also galbitang. VisitKorea wording: “said to be one of Suwon's top three galbi restaurants.” ☎ +82-31-211-8434 · bonsuwon.co.kr

name: Yeonpo Galbi (연포갈비)
notes: VisitKorea: remodeled public bath/inn (chimney kept). Wanggalbi; galbitang lunch only on weekdays, often sells out. Mid-afternoon break. ☎ +82-31-255-1337

name: Kabojung (가보정)
notes: VisitKorea lists it among Suwon's top three galbi restaurants: saenggalbi, yangnyeom galbi, yukhoe; doenjang jjigae; dessert of mini yakgwa and sujeonggwa. ☎ +82-2-1600-3883 · kabojung.co.kr
hours: Weekdays 11:30–21:30 / Sat & public holidays 11:00–22:00 / Sun 11:00–21:30. Open year-round.

name: Leenakyeong Songtan Budaejjigae (이나경송탄부대찌개)
notes: VisitKorea: single dish — special budae jjigae (ox-bone broth); portions for two or more. ☎ +82-31-223-7893

name: Suwon Chicken Street (수원통닭거리) — the alley
notes: VisitKorea: ~100 m alley, about 11 fried-whole-chicken shops; original stall from 1970. Names VisitKorea prints: Maehyang Tongdak, Yongseong Tongdak, Jinmi Tongdak. No official hours for those individual shops — do not treat the street's 24-hour field as any one shop's hours. ☎ +82-31-228-4672 (Suwon tourist information)
hours: Open 24 hr / year-round (street listing). Confirm the shop you enter.

name: Nostalgic Dalgona (추억의달고나)
notes: VisitKorea: make-and-eat dalgona (sugar candy). Near Hwaseong / Paldalmun. ☎ +82-507-1381-4655

name: Suwon Yeongdong Market (수원 영동시장)
notes: VisitKorea: market near Paldalmun since 1917; ~300 stores (hanbok, fabric, clothing, daily goods, food). Hours are the market window — individual food stalls vary. ☎ +82-31-251-0171
hours: 10:00–20:00. Closed the 1st and 15th of every month.

name: Sutgol Won Naengmyeon (숯골원냉면)
notes: Pyeongyang-style naengmyeon run by the same family for four generations. The broth is a blend of dongchimi (radish-water kimchi) and chicken stock, and the noodles are made with Pyeongchang buckwheat. The "National Baeknyeon Gage" and "founded 1954" claims in earlier drafts are not on the official listing and have been removed.
hours: 11:00–20:00. Break 15:30–16:30. Closed New Year's Day, Seollal day and Chuseok day.

name: OC Kalguksu / Ossi Kalguksu (오씨칼국수)
notes: Kalguksu in a broth built on surf clams and anchovies — Daejeon is Korea's kalguksu city and this is one of its standard-bearers. Two corrections: earlier drafts placed it in "Central Jungang-ro" (wrong district) and listed a 15:00–16:30 break that the official listing does not show. The old "Official Listing" link pointed at a Daejeon festival page, not at this restaurant.

name: Daeseon Kalguksu Dunsan Main Store (대선칼국수 둔산본점)
notes: VisitKorea: established 1954; clam broth with crown daisy and perilla powder; also bibim guksu and suyuk. ☎ +82-42-471-0316

name: Samdaejjae Jeontong Kalguksu (삼대째전통칼국수)
notes: VisitKorea: hanu-bone kalguksu, suyuk; kongguksu in summer. ☎ +82-42-257-5432

name: Sindo Kalguksu Main Store (신도칼국수 본점)
notes: VisitKorea: established 1961; beef-bone and anchovy broth with perilla powder; also suyuk and dubu duruchigi. Next door to Samdaejjae. Holiday field: irregular closures — call. ☎ +82-42-253-6799

name: Buchu Haemul Kalguksu Sikdang (부추해물칼국수식당)
notes: VisitKorea: chive-and-seafood kalguksu; chicken-and-vegetable broth two hours; pair with jjukkumi. Not downtown — Sintanjin. ☎ +82-42-934-5656

name: Sariwon Myeonok Main Store (사리원면옥 본점)
notes: Moved out of the Jajangmyeon section — this is not a Korean-Chinese restaurant. Its main dish is Pyeongyang naengmyeon; galbitang and so-bulgogi (Hanwoo bulgogi) are the other signatures. The "founded 1951, four generations" claim in earlier drafts is not on the official listing. Instagram: @sariwon52
hours: 11:00–21:30. Closed the day of and day before Seollal and Chuseok.

name: Taepyeong Sogukbap (태평소국밥)
notes: Sogukbap — beef-and-radish soup with rice — plus yuksashimi (beef tartare) and someori suyuk. Useful for a late arrival or an early train. The "Daejeon's #1 comfort food landmark" line in earlier drafts was unsourced. Earlier drafts also carried a malformed VisitKorea URL; the working one is below.
hours: Open 24 hours. Closed for the Seollal and Chuseok holidays.

name: Byeolcheonji Sikdang (별천지식당)
notes: VisitKorea: oribaeksuk (whole duck with cordyceps/herbs), native-chicken baeksuk, herbal galbitang. Pond-side. Far from the station core — plan a ride. ☎ +82-42-271-0207

name: Gaecheon Sikdang (개천식당)
notes: VisitKorea: handmade Hamgyeong-do mandu; manduguk with boiled pork and glass noodles; also gukbap and steamed/fried mandu. ☎ +82-42-256-1003

name: Baekcheonjip Sikdang (백천집식당)
notes: VisitKorea: sundae gukbap in a hot-pot broth; sundae also sold alone. ☎ +82-42-226-0140
hours: 09:00–19:00. Closed the second Sunday of every month.

name: Gangnam Myeonok Dunsan Branch (강남면옥 둔산점)
notes: VisitKorea listing for this Dunsan address only (the name is used elsewhere). Sogalbijjim, galbitang, hoe naengmyeon. Near City Hall. ☎ +82-42-472-9996

name: Hanbat Sikdang (한밭식당)
notes: VisitKorea: opened 1955; beef-bone broth simmered over five hours; sohanmari tang, seolleongtang, doganitang, galbitang, suyuk. ☎ +82-42-256-1566

name: Sonamujip (소나무집)
notes: VisitKorea: ojingeo jjigae; most diners add noodles (ojingeo kalguksu). Near Sungsimdang. ☎ +82-42-256-1464
hours: 11:30–21:00. Break 15:30–17:30. Closed the 1st & 3rd Monday of each month.

name: Sungsimdang Main Store (성심당 본점)
notes: Founded 1956 near Daejeon Station selling steamed jjinbbang; today it bakes roughly 400 varieties. The two things to queue for are twigim soboro (deep-fried streusel bun) and the pantalong leek bread. Founding year is confirmed by the official listing; the "Daejeon's Taste #1" ranking in earlier drafts was not, and has been removed.

category: Byeongcheon Sundae (병천순대) — the reason to come
name: Cheonghwa-jip (청화집)
notes: VisitKorea: opened early 1950s at Aunae Market with no signboard; a county official assigned the name for tax registration. Fourth-generation couple. Signature sundae-gukbap; also modeum-sundae. Parking. ☎ 041-564-1558. A Baeknyeon Gage label is not on the official listing and is not used here.
hours: Weekdays 09:00–17:00 / Weekends 08:30–17:00. Closed Mondays, and for the Seollal and Chuseok holidays.

category: Byeongcheon Sundae (병천순대) — the reason to come
name: Chungnam-jip Sundae (충남집순대)
notes: The other house VisitKorea names as an originator of Byeongcheon sundae — directly across the road from Cheonghwa-jip, so if one has a queue, walk ten metres. Unfrozen pork small intestine, cooked with a pork-rib broth simmered six hours. Signature sundae; sundae-gukbap also served. Parking available. ☎ 041-564-1079

category: Byeongcheon Sundae (병천순대) — the reason to come
name: Aunae Jangteo Sundae (아우내 장터순대)
notes: Opened 1994; the TV-famous one of the street. Beef-bone broth made fresh each morning with vegetables. Beyond the standard sundae-gukbap there is eolkeuni sundae-gukbap (spicy) and a kimchi-spicy version. Large car park in front, and it is the closest of the three to Mokcheon IC. ☎ 041-564-5949

category: Byeongcheon Sundae (병천순대) — the reason to come
name: Byeongcheon Sundae Street (천안 병천순대거리) — the street itself
notes: VisitKorea: about 20 sundae specialists. Hours vary by shop. Daily sundae-gukbap trade from 1968. ☎ 041-521-5169

name: Dongsunwon Seonghwan Main Branch (동순원 성환본점)
notes: Open since 1960 on the same spot. The house dish is jjamppong, not jajangmyeon — heavy on seafood and deliberately lightly seasoned. Jajangmyeon, udon, tangsuyuk and yangjangpi are also served. Three corrections: earlier drafts put it in "Seonghwan" without a district (it is Seobuk-gu, not Dongnam-gu), listed it as "Daily 11:00–21:00" (wrong on both the closing time and the closing day), and filed it under jajangmyeon. No parking. ☎ 041-581-2070

name: Deogwon Kkorigomtang Bangchitang (덕원꼬리곰탕방치탕)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 4 Jun 2026): oxtail soup (kkori-gomtang) and bangchi-tang, made from the hip bone; the Korean listing also names jung-tomak, ox-head suyuk and ox-foot suyuk. Generous bone-in portions. ☎ +82-2-2634-8663

name: Hamheung Naengmyeon (함흥냉면)
notes: VisitKorea: serving Hamheung-style naengmyeon since 1967, now second generation. House dish is hoe-naengmyeon topped with aged raw skate; mul and bibim naengmyeon and a meat–rice-cake–mandu soup are also listed. ☎ +82-2-2678-2722

name: Haeju Naengmyeon (해주냉면)
notes: VisitKorea: a two-dish house — mul naengmyeon and a very spicy bibim naengmyeon — with mulmandu and boiled eggs on the side. Garlic-heavy sauce; the page suggests warm broth or an egg if the heat is too much. ☎ +82-2-424-7192
hours: 11:30–21:00 (last order 20:30). Closed Sundays, Seollal & Chuseok holidays.

name: Neungrado Myeongdong Branch (능라도 명동점)
notes: Visit Seoul (published & edited 12 Aug 2026): Pyeongyang naengmyeon with buckwheat milled and cut in-house daily and a 1++ hanu broth; also eobuk-jaengban, nokdu-jijim, bulgogi. 200 seats, private room for up to 40 (room charge, 4+ people). Five minutes' walk from Myeongdong or Euljiro 1-ga stations. ☎ +82-507-1338-3989 · neungrado-myeongdong.com

name: Joseonok (조선옥)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 3 Jun 2026): so-galbi marinated a full day in aged soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic and sugar, then charcoal-grilled. The page says the restaurant opened before the Korean War and was one of the top three houses in the Euljiro area into the mid-1970s. Exit 6 of Euljiro 3-ga, 67 m. ☎ +82-2-2266-0333

name: Daepyeong Galbi (대평갈비)
notes: VisitKorea: jumbo beef ribs and spareribs, plus hanu yukhoe, in a large hall built for groups. Well north of the centre in Pyeongchang-dong — a taxi ride from Gyeongbokgung, not a walk. The listing prints no closing day, so confirm before travelling out. ☎ +82-2-395-5288
hours: 11:30–21:30 (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Gwanghwamun Gukbap (광화문국밥)
michelin: None — VisitKorea prints no MICHELIN note for this restaurant.
notes: VisitKorea: dwaeji-gukbap from chef Park Chan-il, using only black-pork loin and shoulder for a clean, deep broth; also dwaeji suyuk and pi-sundae. Cards accepted. Note the long afternoon break. ☎ +82-2-738-5688

name: Tongdwaeji Duruchigi (통돼지두루치기)
notes: VisitKorea: duruchigi — pork and vegetables stir-fried in gochujang — with pork-and-kimchi stew as the listed house dish. Same block as the Dongdaemun dak-hanmari alley, so it is an easy swap if Jin Ok-hwa has a queue. The listing prints no closing day. ☎ +82-2-2266-9290
hours: 10:00–22:00 (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Myeongdong Busanjib (명동부산집)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 30 Jun 2026): halal Korean cooking in the middle of Myeongdong — jjigae, bibimbap, ganjang-gejang, prepared to halal standards. The page records Muslim cooks on staff and no alcohol sold. ☎ +82-10-3142-0278

name: Myeongdong Chaeum Hanjongshik (명동채움 한정식)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 30 Jun 2026): halal hanjeongsik — a set meal of 18 side dishes with soup and stew, prepared fresh daily. The page records alcohol on sale and no Muslim cook on staff, so check against your own requirements. Basement level two. ☎ +82-2-779-9998

name: Haeundae Gaya Milmyeon (해운대 가야밀면)
notes: VisitKorea: founded May 1998. Brisket, shank, chicken feet, ginger, onion, garlic and herbs simmered 48 hours, then the broth aged over a year. Also bibim-myeon and mandu. Different restaurant from Gaya Halmae Milmyeon (Yeonje-gu) and Halmae Gaya Milmyeon (Nampo). ☎ +82-507-1404-9404 · pgy13490.modoo.at

name: 1969 Buwondong Kalguksu Busan Main Branch (1969부원동칼국수 부산본점)
notes: Visit Busan: kalguksu heaped with oysters and scallops bought at the morning auction; the portal says the kitchen works in limited daily quantities and usually runs out around 18:00, so treat the 19:30 close as a ceiling, not a promise. ☎ 0507-1477-9925
hours: 11:00–19:30. Open every day (sells out early — Visit Busan says around 18:00).

name: Pyeongan-do Jokbal (평안도족발)
notes: Visit Busan: jokbal house in the same spot for over 30 years; the portal credits it with clean, odour-free pork hocks. Naengchae jokbal (cold-tossed, a Busan speciality) and garlic jokbal are the other two orders. Open late — a Haeundae after-dinner option. ☎ +82-51-741-6568

name: Gwangalli Eonyang Bulgogi Busanjip
notes: Visit Busan: Eonyang-style bulgogi — the Ulsan regional style, hand-chopped beef pressed into patties — from 100% Korean beef, with the owner's own organic produce. Roughly 30 years in business per the portal. Accessible facilities and accessible parking are marked on the listing. The official English page prints no Korean name, so search the address on Naver Map rather than a transliteration. ☎ +82-51-754-1004

name: Sinchang Gukbap (신창국밥)
notes: Visit Busan: established 1969 in Sinchang-dong at Gukje Market, and described by the portal as the origin of clear-broth dwaeji-gukbap. Traditional toryeom service (rice warmed by repeated pours of hot broth) and house-made North Korean-style sundae. ☎ 051-244-1112

name: Gayapocha Seonjigukbap Main Branch (가야포차선지국밥 본점)
notes: Visit Busan: open 24 hours for over 30 years, serving sugure-gukbap (beef skin lining) and seonji-gukbap (beef blood curd) — dishes that are hard to find elsewhere. Drinking dishes from 16:00. The genuinely late-night option on this list. ☎ 051-894-6921
hours: Open 24 hours. Closed for two days during the holidays.

name: Pohang Dwaeji Gukbap (포항돼지국밥)
notes: VisitKorea: over 50 years on the Seomyeon Market food street, a few doors from Songjeong Samdae Gukbap. Dwaeji-gukbap plus samgyeop-gukbap, sundae-gukbap and suyuk baekban. Opens at 05:00 — the breakfast pick of this guide. ☎ +82-51-807-5439

name: Geumsubokguk Haeundae Branch (금수복국)
notes: Visit Busan: 50-year-old bokguk (pufferfish soup) house, described by the portal as the original. Two floors keep different hours — the ground floor runs around the clock, the second-floor pufferfish restaurant does not. Sauces made in-house. ☎ 051-742-3600
hours: 1F open 24 hours, every day. 2F 11:00–22:00 (break 15:00–17:00; last orders 13:30 and 20:30).

name: Jeju Bokguk (제주복국)
notes: Visit Busan: bokguk portioned into individual bowls at the table rather than served in a communal earthen pot; the portal calls it one of the city's benchmark pufferfish houses and notes the classic, spacious hall. Pairs with a Yeongdo day (Huinnyeoul, Taejongdae). ☎ +82-51-405-5050

name: Hanmaeum Naengmyeon (한마음냉면)
notes: VisitKorea: Pyeongyang-style naengmyeon in a light broth. The listed standout is kimchi-bibim — arongsatae suyuk (boiled beef heel) tossed with kimchi — eaten alongside the cold noodles, with hot broth served to cut the heat. Also bibim naengmyeon, suyuk and, in winter, manduguk. Jinjam is in the far south-west of the city, well past Yuseong. ☎ +82-42-543-9384
hours: 10:00–19:30. November–February: closed the 1st & 3rd Wednesday of the month.

name: Ojang-dong Hamheung Naengmyeon (오장동 함흥냉면)
notes: Started by Han Hye-seon, who came south from Hamgyeong-do during the Korean War; Visit Seoul (edited 3 Aug 2026) credits it with introducing Hamheung naengmyeon to the rest of the country. House dish is bibim naengmyeon with raw-fish topping; also mul naengmyeon, suyuk, mandu. The two official sources differ on the break: VisitKorea prints a daily 15:30–17:00 break, Visit Seoul prints the break on Mon/Thu/Fri only. ☎ +82-2-2267-9500
hours: 11:00–20:00. Break 15:30–17:00 (Mon, Thu–Fri per Visit Seoul; daily per VisitKorea). Closed Tuesdays, Seollal & Chuseok.

name: Gaeseong Mandu Koong (개성만두 궁)
notes: Gaeseong-style mandu for more than 30 years; the founder was a Korean War refugee and her granddaughters now run it. Mandu jeongol (hot pot for 2–3) and manduguk are the standards; sells out some evenings. This entry was previously withheld from the guide because Visit Seoul and MICHELIN printed different hours — VisitKorea now publishes a full, dated schedule, which is what is shown here, and the page itself warns hours can change. Earlier drafts called it a Bib Gourmand; that badge is not re-verified here. ☎ +82-2-733-9240 · koong.co.kr
hours: Weekdays & Sat 11:30–21:30 (last order 20:50) / Sun 11:30–20:00 (last order 19:20). Break 15:00–16:00. Open year-round.

name: Jongro Seolleongtang (종로설렁탕)
notes: VisitKorea: ox-bone soup house on Jongno; suyuk hot pot is the other order. Open around the clock — one of the few 24-hour options in the Jongno 3-ga area, useful after a late arrival. The listing prints no closing day. ☎ +82-2-2271-3820
hours: Open 24 hours (00:00–24:00) (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Oegojip Seolleongtang (외고집설렁탕)
michelin: VisitKorea says recognised by the MICHELIN Guide — no year given, and this is not a 2026 Bib Gourmand claim.
notes: Seolleongtang made only from Grade 1 hanu, plus suyuk and yukgaejang. Near COEX, Bongeunsa and Seonjeongneung, so it works as a Gangnam lunch. ☎ +82-2-567-5225 · oegojip.modoo.at

name: Jinmi Pyeongyang Naengmyeon (진미평양냉면)
michelin: VisitKorea: MICHELIN Guide Seoul 2023 listing. Not a 2026 Bib Gourmand.
notes: Pyeongyang naengmyeon from chef Im Se-kwon, who trained in Jangchung-dong: clean broth, chewy noodles, with jeyuk, mandu and bulgogi alongside. VisitKorea warns about long queues. ☎ +82-2-515-3469 · jinmipy.modoo.at

name: Won Gopchang (원곱창)
notes: Grilled beef tripe and pork intestines, with a pork bulgogi set as the non-offal option. Walking distance from Gyeongbokgung, in the Sejong Village food street area. Field conflict on the page: hours are printed as 11:00–23:00 while the holiday field says “Open 24/7” — read that as *no closing day*, not as 24-hour opening. ☎ +82-2-722-2934
hours: 11:00–23:00. Holiday field reads “Open 24/7” (i.e. no regular closing day) — confirm before a late visit.

name: Samgyeopsal Jeonmunjeom Daetongnyeong (삼겹살전문점대통령)
address: 1F, 249-24 Jangchungdan-ro, Jung-gu (Dongdaemun History & Culture Park side)
notes: VisitKorea: samgyeopsal aged in bamboo tubes, served with kimchi and wraps; blue-crab doenjang jjigae and naengmyeon round out the table. The listing calls it good value. Long day — open to 23:00, year-round. ☎ +82-507-1353-2287

name: Vegan Kitchen
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 29 Jun 2026): vegan Korean cooking a few minutes from Myeongdong Station Exit 3 — vegan stir-fried noodles and hot-plate soft tofu rice are the signatures. Alcohol sold; no Muslim cook on staff per the page. The Korean name is not printed on the official page, so search the address on Naver Map. ☎ +82-2-777-8819

name: KAMPUNGKU
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 30 Jun 2026): halal Malaysian kitchen — nasi goreng and nasi lemak from a Malaysian chef — that also cooks Korean dishes (including budae jjigae) with halal ingredients. Page records Muslim cooks on staff and no alcohol. Same Myeongdong lane as Vegan Kitchen and MaeHwa. ☎ +82-507-1380-9249

name: MaeHwa Lamb Skewers Myeongdong
notes: Visit Seoul (published 17 Apr 2026, edited 29 Jun 2026): lamb specialist using meat from sheep under a year old — lamb chops and sweet-and-sour crispy lamb. Not Korean cuisine; listed here as the late-night option on the Toegye-ro 20-gil lane. Alcohol sold, no Muslim cook per the page. ☎ +82-2-772-9289

name: 100.1.pyeongnaeng (백일평냉)
notes: Visit Busan: Pyeongyang naengmyeon built on beef broth, salt and 80% buckwheat noodles; house-made North Korean-style manduguk and hanwoo bulgogi are the other orders. Short dinner window — the kitchen closes at 19:00. ☎ 051-625-5515

name: Halmaejip Hoeguksu (할매집회국수)
notes: Visit Busan: more than 70 years in the old city centre, serving hoe-guksu — cold noodles in a spicy sauce topped with stingray. Hoe bibim-guksu and hoe bibimbap are the two orders. Closes at 19:00 and shuts on two Tuesdays a month. ☎ 051-246-4741
hours: 10:30–19:00. Closed the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month.

name: Hongseongbang (홍성방)
address: 16 Jungang-daero 179beon-gil, Dong-gu (Busan Chinatown, by Busan Station)
notes: Visit Busan: three generations, over 50 years in Busan's Chinatown. The boiled dumplings are famous enough that locals call them “Yeongju-dong water dumplings”; ohyang-jangyuk (five-spice sliced steamed pork) is the other speciality. Walkable from Busan Station. ☎ 051-467-5398

name: Marine Buffet (마린뷔페)
notes: VisitKorea: buffet with a panoramic view over Busan Port — Korean, Japanese, Chinese and Western dishes plus an on-site grill corner for galbi. Two fixed sittings only, and closed Mondays; not a drop-in. Cards accepted. ☎ +82-51-466-3800

name: Gyeryong Samgyetang (계룡삼계탕)
notes: VisitKorea: samgyetang built on yak-nokdu samgyetang — mung bean and more than ten medicinal herbs — served in a hot pot. Also neungi-nokdu samgyetang and ot-baeksuk. Same Jinjam neighbourhood as Hanmaeum Naengmyeon, in the far south-west of the city. ☎ +82-42-546-0515

name: Hanbang Samgyetang (한방삼계탕)
notes: VisitKorea: a one-dish house — hanbang samgyetang, chicken slow-cooked with medicinal herbs, served with a ginseng-liquor aperitif and kkakdugi. Note the twice-monthly Sunday closure, which is easy to miss. ☎ +82-42-861-6127
hours: 11:00–21:00. Closed the 2nd and 4th Sunday of every month.

name: Pungnyeon Samgyetang (풍년삼계탕)
address: 407 Gyejok-ro, Dong-gu (by the Daejeon Terminal Complex)
notes: VisitKorea: samgyetang served in a hot pot so it stays hot to the last spoonful, with a layer of porridge under the chicken; pajeon and mungmuchim on the side. Next to the express bus terminal — a practical first or last meal in Daejeon. ☎ +82-42-632-5757

name: Gugu Jeonbok Samgyetang (구구전복삼계탕)
notes: VisitKorea: samgyetang with abalone and neungi mushrooms, finished with nurungji; grilled duck and abalone dishes also listed. The holiday field is printed untranslated as 연중무휴 — that means open year-round. ☎ +82-42-623-9952
hours: 11:00–21:00. Open year-round (holiday field printed in Korean as 연중무휴).

name: Jangkalguksu (장칼국수)
address: 49 Cheonancheon 8-gil, Dongnam-gu (Sinbu-dong) — Korean address as printed: 천안시 동남구 천안천8길 49
notes: Chungnam Tourism (the provincial portal): jang-kalguksu — knife-cut noodles in a fermented-soy-and-chilli broth — with hand-pulled noodles and a house pork cutlet as the second order. Portal warns of queues at weekends and lunch, and of tight parking. Near Sinbu-dong / Shinsegae, walkable from Cheonan Station's bus corridor. ☎ 041-555-3567
hours: 11:00–20:15. Break 15:00–16:00. No closing day (portal: 휴무 없음).

name: Jeongsang Galbi (정상갈비)
address: 107 Yuryang-ro, Dongnam-gu — Korean address as printed: 충청남도 천안시 동남구 유량로 107
notes: Chungnam Tourism: charcoal-grilled dwaeji galbi from domestic pork, marinated in a house sauce; galbitang and beef bulgogi also served, and mul naengmyeon comes as the after-meal course. Large car park, hillside view, built for groups. The portal leaves the closing-day field blank — call before travelling out. ☎ 0507-1356-7226 · jungsangfood.modoo.at
hours: 11:00–21:00. Closing day not printed on the portal — confirm by phone.

name: Galjae Sanjang (갈재산장)
address: 348 Haesu-gil, Dongnam-gu (Gwangdeok-myeon) — Korean address as printed: 충청남도 천안시 동남구 해수길 348 갈채산장식당
notes: Chungnam Tourism: valley restaurant below Gwangdeoksan, known for neungi dak-baeksuk (whole chicken with neungi mushroom) and neungi duck baeksuk, plus dak-bokkeumtang and ot-dak. Country outing rather than a city meal — about 20 km south-west of Cheonan Station, and the portal recommends booking. Closing-day field is blank. ☎ 0507-1335-4231
hours: 09:00–20:00. Closing day not printed on the portal — book ahead.

name: Igamyeonok (이가면옥)
notes: VisitKorea: Hamheung-style naengmyeon house in Seochon; the listed house dish is hoe-naengmyeon (cold noodles with raw fish), with suyuk alongside. Two doors from Won Gopchang on the same Jahamun-ro 1-gil lane, so the two make an easy Seochon pair. ☎ +82-2-3210-3337
hours: 11:00–20:30 (last order 20:00) (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Well-being Sujebi (웰빙수제비)
notes: VisitKorea calls it a hidden lunch spot for Jongno office workers. House dish is sujebi in perilla-seed broth; a seafood noodle soup is the other order. Closes at 20:00 and shuts on Tuesdays — not a late dinner. ☎ +82-2-747-2436

name: Eunhangnamujip (은행나무집)
notes: VisitKorea: an office-worker favourite for marinated grilled beef ribs, with boneless short rib as the other cut. The page lists it as open around the clock — one of very few 24-hour galbi options near Dongdaemun. ☎ +82-2-2273-0160
hours: Open 24 hours (00:00–24:00). No closing day (holiday field reads “Open 24/7”).

name: Busan Agujjim Gulbossam (부산아구찜굴보쌈)
notes: VisitKorea: spicy braised monkfish (agu-jjim) plus gul-bossam — boiled pork and oysters wrapped in kimchi, a winter dish that suits a November trip. Note the long afternoon break and the 20:00 last order. ☎ +82-2-764-2373

name: Chamchi Maeul (참치마을)
notes: VisitKorea: tuna specialist — sliced raw tuna by the cut, plus a raw-fish bibimbap. Filed by VisitKorea as Japanese cuisine, not Korean. Next door to Busan Agujjim Gulbossam. ☎ +82-2-742-1671
hours: 11:00–22:00. Holiday field reads “Open 24/7” (i.e. no regular closing day).

name: Sigoljeonjip (시골전집)
address: 123 Jong-ro, Jongno-gu (Jongno 3-ga — same building as Well-being Sujebi)
notes: VisitKorea: cheap-and-cheerful jeon house by Jongno 3-ga Station — haemul-pajeon (seafood and spring onion pancake) with kongnamul-gukbap to follow. Open to 22:00, last order 21:00; a jeon-and-makgeolli stop after the Jongno 3-ga pocha street. ☎ +82-2-742-8525
hours: 11:00–22:00 (last order 21:00) (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Bukmun Seafood (북문 해물탕)
notes: VisitKorea (halal-friendly listing): Korean seafood house whose listed dishes are spicy seafood stew (haemul-tang) and braised seafood, both sized for a table rather than one person. Marked pork-free with a halal menu, but the page says there is no prayer room. Walkable from Janganmun, so it pairs with the Hwaseong north-wall stretch. ☎ +82-31-243-2441
hours: 11:00–22:00. Closed the 1st Monday of each month.

name: Chungmyung (청명쭈꾸미 철판구이)
notes: VisitKorea (halal-friendly listing): griddled jjukkumi — spicy stir-fried baby octopus — served with rice. Marked halal menu and pork-free; no prayer room. Seven parking spaces. Gwonseon-gu is south-west of the fortress, so this is a car/bus stop rather than a Hwaseong walk. ☎ +82-31-239-7892
hours: 10:00–22:00 (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Swoyambhu (수엠부)
notes: VisitKorea: Indian and Nepalese cooking — chicken tikka, vegetarian curry set, chicken chow mein. Halal menu, pork-free, prayer room available, 110 seats. A five-minute walk from Suwon Station, which makes it the most practical non-galbi meal in the city for a day trip. ☎ +82-31-258-3305

name: Naan (난)
notes: VisitKorea: Indian kitchen in the Ingye-dong restaurant district — tandoori chicken by the half or whole bird, garlic naan. Halal menu and prayer room; 100 seats and seven parking spaces. Near Suwon City Hall Station rather than the fortress. ☎ +82-31-237-1090
hours: 11:00–22:00 (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Om Restaurant Gwanggyo Branch (옴레스토랑 광교점)
address: #B223 Raon Zone, 2F, Avenue France, 85 Centraltown-ro, Yeongtong-gu (Gwanggyo)
notes: VisitKorea: Indian restaurant in the Avenue France mall at Gwanggyo — tandoori chicken and vegetable biryani are the listed dishes. Halal menu, pork-free, prayer room, 100 parking spaces and coach parking. Out at Gwanggyo, not central Suwon. ☎ +82-31-305-8848 · omfood.kr
hours: 10:00–22:00 (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Myeonchaeum (면채움)
notes: Visit Busan: milmyeon made with five-grain noodles, a 48-hour broth and a sauce built on fruit and vegetables; bibim-mandu is the local nostalgia order. Up by PNU rather than downtown. ☎ +82-507-1468-4448

name: Jang Seong Hyang (장성향)
notes: VisitKorea: Chinatown restaurant best known for the dumplings eaten by Oh Dae-su in Park Chan-wook's _Oldboy_. Cards accepted, take-out available. Same quarter as Hongseongbang, so the two make a Chinatown pair. ☎ +82-51-467-4496

name: Jeongjitgan (정짓간)
notes: Visit Busan: named after the Gyeongsang dialect word for “kitchen”; the dwaeji-gukbap broth is boiled 48 hours in a cauldron, and you choose pork belly or jowl, plus topping, temperature and spice level. Makguksu is the other order. Open around the clock. ☎ +82-507-1411-2900
hours: Open 24 hours. Closed on public holidays.

name: Woojung's Bibimbap (우정)
notes: VisitKorea: dolsot bibimbap specialist by Seomyeon's Street of Youth, with yeolmu (young radish kimchi) and yeolmu-tuna versions. A cheap, fast, vegetable-heavy break from the gukbap-and-barbecue rotation. ☎ +82-51-802-6282

name: Ilbeonji Jagalchi Sangomjangeo (일번지자갈치산곰장어)
notes: VisitKorea: gomjangeo (hagfish) grilled to order inside Haeundae Market — yangnyeom (spicy), sogeum (salt) and whole-grilled versions, and the kitchen will do it over briquettes on request. Busan's signature late-night grill; open to 01:00. ☎ +82-51-743-5340

name: Byeogodong (벽오동)
address: 138 Hyanggyo 1-gil, Dongnam-gu (Yuryang-dong) — Korean address as printed: 천안시 동남구 향교1길 138
notes: Chungnam Tourism: boribap (barley rice) set meal — barley rice with namul, a stew and a spread of side dishes, listed as the only main. Quiet setting on the edge of town near Cheonan Hyanggyo, with parking. The portal notes a break time exists but does not print the times; a blog on the same page says 15:30–17:00, which is *not* an official figure. ☎ 0507-1400-5081
hours: 10:30–20:30. Closed Sundays. (A break time exists; the portal does not print the hours.)

name: Kkachi Bokjip (까치복집)
address: 13-7 Baekseok 3-ro, Seobuk-gu (Baekseok-dong) — Korean address as printed: 천안시 서북구 백석3로 13-7
notes: Chungnam Tourism: pufferfish specialist — tojang bokguk (soybean-paste pufferfish soup) made to a patented recipe, plus bok-jiri, bok-twigim and bok-bulgogi, cooked by a certified Korean master chef per the portal. Bok is the Korean hangover soup of choice; useful after a soju night. ☎ 041-551-1258

name: Dongmin Mokjang (동민목장)
address: 154 Wangrim-gil, Seobuk-gu (Seonghwan-eup) — Korean address as printed: 충청남도 천안시 서북구 왕림길 154
notes: Chungnam Tourism: a large café set in a pear orchard in Seonghwan, best known for the blossom in spring and used as a filming location for the drama *Queen of Tears*. Coffee, house lattes and desserts; roof terrace and annexe are no-kids zones, pets allowed. Seasonal hours. Combine with Dongsunwon in Seonghwan rather than a Byeongcheon trip. ☎ 0507-1437-7745
hours: April–November 11:00–20:00 / December–March 11:00–18:00. No closing day printed on the portal.

name: Seoul Wonjo Agujjim (서울 원조아구찜)
notes: VisitKorea (Muslim-friendly listing): agujjim — monkfish braised with beansprouts in a chilli sauce — plus a mixed braised-seafood version, both sized for sharing. Marked *muslim friendly* only: the page claims no halal menu, no prayer room, so treat that flag loosely. Open to 01:00, which makes it one of the few late Jongno sit-down options. Ten parking spaces. ☎ +82-2-764-4207
hours: 10:00–01:00 (next day) (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Sejong Village Chicken (세종 마을 치킨)
notes: VisitKorea: Seochon fried-chicken house listed as Korean food and marked pork-free; the two listed dishes are plain fried chicken and soy-sauce chicken. Opens at 14:00 and runs to 01:00 — an evening stop, not a lunch. Same Jahamun-ro 1-gil lane as Igamyeonok and Won Gopchang, so the three sit within a two-minute walk. 54 seats, no prayer room. ☎ +82-2-725-9293
hours: 14:00–01:00 (next day) (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Pooja 2 (뿌자 2)
notes: VisitKorea (halal listing): Indian and Nepalese kitchen on the 4th floor — stir-fried lamb and chicken biryani are the listed dishes. Halal menu and pork-free; no prayer room. 40 seats. Closest halal-listed option to the Myeongdong/Euljiro hotel strip apart from the Itaewon cluster. ☎ +82-2-2274-2922 · pooja.fordining.kr
hours: 11:00–15:00 / 17:00–23:00 (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Itaewon Kitchen (이태원 키친)
address: 2F, 34 Usadan-ro, Yongsan-gu (Usadan-ro, below Seoul Central Mosque)
notes: VisitKorea (halal listing): Malaysian cooking on the Usadan-ro slope under the Seoul Central Mosque; the listed set is nasi goreng with ayam. Flagged self-certified halal, alcohol-free, pork-free, Muslim chef — the fullest set of flags of any Seoul listing we have checked. 50 seats, no prayer room on site (the mosque is a two-minute walk up the hill). ☎ +82-2-3785-2468
hours: 11:30–23:00 (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Zaffran (자프란)
notes: VisitKorea (halal listing): small Indian room off Usadan-ro 10-gil, 30 seats; chicken tikka makhni and a green salad are the listed dishes. Self-certified halal, alcohol-free, pork-free, Muslim chef. The one entry in this pass with a printed closing day — Wednesdays — and it shuts at 21:30, earlier than its neighbours. ☎ +82-2-3785-3571

name: AANGAN (아건)
notes: VisitKorea (halal listing): Indian and Nepalese kitchen by Ewha Womans University — chicken vindaloo, samosa, tandoori chicken. Halal menu, pork-free, and a prayer room on site, which is rare outside Itaewon. 50 seats. ☎ +82-2-364-8771 · aangan.modoo.at
hours: 11:00–22:00 (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Ezindia (이지인디아)
address: 3F, 20 Yonsei-ro, Seodaemun-gu (Sinchon, on the Yonsei approach)
notes: VisitKorea (halal listing): third-floor Indian/Nepalese room on the Yonsei-ro student strip in Sinchon, also listed as doing a buffet; tandoori chicken and chicken biryani are the named dishes. Halal menu, pork-free; no prayer room. Only 30 seats. ☎ +82-2-393-7771 · instagram.com/ezindia
hours: 11:00–22:00 (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: Busak Yakkong Milmyeon (부산약콩밀면)
notes: Visit Busan: a milmyeon house that builds its broth on natural brine from yakkong soybeans, hamcho (glasswort) and hijiki, with vinegar made from Gijang kelp — 40 years of recipe work per the portal. Mul and mulbibim milmyeon are the two listed bowls. Portal menu prices are not copied here. ☎ 051-611-1231

name: Ha Gi-yeon Jinju Naengmyeon (하기연진주냉면)
notes: Visit Busan: Jinju-style naengmyeon — a seafood broth of anchovy, clam and kelp, topped with yukjeon (beef pancake) — which the portal describes as a rare speciality only a few trained masters cook. Noodles are made with Jeju black buckwheat. Order the mulbibim naengmyeon with a plate of yukjeon. Portal prices not copied. ☎ 051-207-6555

name: Haemul Wangchang Kalguksu (해물왕창칼국수)
notes: Visit Busan: seafood kalguksu whose clams come daily from Goheung in Jeolla, with the dough made and rested each morning. The house bowl is sized for two; a mul milmyeon with yukjeon is the other order. Sasang, so pair it with the intercity bus terminal rather than the beaches. Portal prices not copied. ☎ 0507-1357-2579

name: Jungang Momil (중앙모밀)
notes: Visit Busan: open since 1956 and specialising in buckwheat noodles and udon for over 60 years — the portal notes three generations of the same Busan families eat here. Address is printed on the portal as "9-1, 49beon-gil, Jungang-daero, Jung-gu". Downtown, so it slots into a Jagalchi/Bupyeong walk. ☎ 051-246-8686

name: Lee Family's Kalguksu (이가네 칼국수)
address: 27 Gwangjang-ro, Sasang-gu (by Sasang Intercity Bus Terminal)
notes: Visit Busan: terminal-side noodle house doing sonkalguksu (hand-cut noodles), large hand-made dumplings and milmyeon. Useful if you are catching an intercity coach out of Sasang. ☎ 051-322-8131

name: Yasumaru (야스마루)
notes: Visit Busan: a Seomyeon noodle bar with no signboard and a permanent queue; the house bowl is *parang guksu*, and a mackerel seaweed roll is the other listed dish. Note the unusual closing pattern — Sundays and the second and fourth Mondays — and the 14:50 lunch cut-off. ☎ 010-7144-7600
hours: 12:00–14:50 / 17:30–21:00. Closed Sundays and the 2nd and 4th Mondays.

name: Uri Dwaejigukbap (우리돼지국밥)
notes: Visit Busan: since 1975, three generations, broth boiled 24 hours and served *toryeom*-style; the kitchen uses the whole pig and will cut whichever part you ask for. Open 24 hours, 365 days — the most useful late-night or pre-dawn gukbap near Busan Station. ☎ 051-468-5623

name: Bugwang Dwaejigukbap (부광돼지국밥)
notes: Visit Busan: over 40 years and three generations; kimchi and kkakdugi are made in-house. Dwaejigukbap and steamed pork are the two listed orders. Note it closes at 19:30 and shuts Sundays and public holidays — the opposite of the 24-hour gukbap houses. Portal prices not copied. ☎ 051-466-1708

name: Halmae Jaecheopguk (할매재첩국)
notes: Visit Busan: jaecheopguk — freshwater-clam soup, the Busan breakfast and hangover cure. The owner started selling it in Gupo in 1950 and moved here about 20 years ago. Opens at 06:00, the earliest opening in this guide. A clam set meal or clam-with-rice are the listed orders. ☎ 0507-1400-7658

name: Wonjo Kkorigomjip (원조꼬리곰집)
notes: Visit Busan: open since 1980; oxtail — steamed hanwoo tail slices and kkori-gomtang — with the skin kept on by a house method for a softer texture. Opens 08:30, so it works as a big breakfast before the Dongnae hot springs. ☎ +82-507-1379-1134
hours: 08:30–21:30 (last order 20:50). Closed Mondays and public holidays.

name: Park Hae-yun Tongyeong Bapsang (박해윤 통영 해물밥상)
notes: Visit Busan: hanjeongsik (full Korean set meal) built on seafood shipped from Tongyeong; the portal notes it is a venue for first birthdays and family occasions, with a large car park. The two listed sets are the seafood set and the bori-gulbi (barley-cured croaker) set. The one entry here that is a sit-down banquet rather than a quick bowl. ☎ 051-525-0120

name: Janganjip (장안집)
notes: Visit Busan: hanok-style duck house beside a mountain stream near Jangansa temple in Gijang — duck bulgogi and duck baeksuk, plus a duck soup the portal singles out. Large car park and private rooms. This is a day trip to the far north-east of the metropolitan area, roughly an hour from Haeundae, not a city meal. ☎ 051-727-1819

name: Lee Family's Tteokbokki (이가네 떡볶이)
notes: Visit Busan: the Bupyeong market tteokbokki stall made nationally famous by TV; the listed orders are a plain serving and a serving with twigim (fritters). Note it is a daytime stop — closes 17:00 and shuts Sundays, so it does not combine with the Bupyeong night market. ☎ 051-245-0413

name: Ori Daega (오리대가)
notes: VisitKorea (halal-friendly listing): a duck house near Paldalmun listed as Korean food and marked pork-free, with a prayer room on site. The named dish is a whole-duck soup with abalone. 250 seats, 50 car spaces and coach parking, so it is built for groups. The only non-galbi, non-Indian Korean entry we have been able to verify inside Suwon. ☎ +82-507-1393-5292
hours: 11:30–15:00 / 17:00–21:30 (no closing day printed on the listing)

name: A-Gate Cafe (에이게이트카페)
address: 183 Dongni 2-gil, Dongnam-gu (Mokcheon-eup) — Korean address as printed: 충청남도 천안시 동남구 동리2길 183
notes: Chungnam Tourism: large bakery café out at Mokcheon with a garden, terrace and a big car park behind; pets welcome. Listed dishes are a bagel-cream-cheese salad and a tomato-cheese oven pasta rather than only coffee. Sits between the Independence Hall of Korea and Yongyeon reservoir, so it is a drive-and-stop after the memorial rather than a city café. The portal leaves the closing-day field blank — call before going. ☎ 0507-1440-2207 · instagram.com/a_gate_cafe
hours: 10:00–22:00. Closing day not printed on the portal — confirm by phone.

name: Jinguk Seolleongtang (진국설렁탕)
notes: VisitKorea: a Korean restaurant in Seongdong-gu whose most famous menu is ox bone soup (seolleongtang); boiled meat slices (suyuk) is the other order. Near Wangsimni Station. ☎ +82-2-2292-4700
hours: 04:00–22:30. (The page intro says "open 24 hours a day" and the holiday field reads "Open 24/7" — read that as no closing day; the printed hours field is 04:00–22:30.)

name: Seongwon Jeonju Kongnamul Gukbap (성원 전주콩나물국밥)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 24 Jun 2026): founded 1937 by Kim So-seon, who introduced kongnamul gukbap (bean-sprout rice soup) to the area; signature dish kongnamul gukbap. Myeongdong Station Exit 8, ~269 m. Same building as Teumsae Ramyeon. ☎ +82-2-777-4284

name: Teumsae Ramyeon (틈새라면)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 4 Jun 2026): Korean-style ramyeon, mostly spicy; bbalgyetteok (pepper-flake, egg and rice-cake) and cold yeolmu ramyeon also listed. This is the Myeongdong shop of a small ramyeon chain — treat these hours as this location's. Same building as Seongwon Jeonju Kongnamul Gukbap. ☎ +82-2-756-5477
hours: Weekdays 10:00–20:00 / weekends & public holidays 11:00–20:00. Closed Seollal & Chuseok.

name: Myeongdong Tonkatsu (명동돈까스)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 8 Jun 2026): the first restaurant to introduce thick Japanese-style pork cutlets to Korea; 30-year history, cordon bleu the most popular item. Not to be confused with Wonjo Namsan Wangdonkkaseu (21 Myeongdong 7-gil). ☎ +82-2-775-5300 · mddongas.co.kr

name: Myeongdong Jjukkumi (명동쭈꾸미)
notes: VisitKorea: jjukkumi (stir-fried baby octopus) and samgyeopsal sets, plus pork galbi and bossam; spicy house style with a self-serve side-dish bar. One minute from Hoehyeon Station (Line 4) Exit 2. ☎ +82-507-1430-0198 · instagram.com/myeongdong.jjukkumi

name: Eun&Jeong Myeongdong Dakgalbi (은앤정명동닭갈비)
notes: VisitKorea: dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken), with cheese and garlic-soy versions; rice cakes, sweet potato, noodles and fried rice can be added. Also budae jjigae, makguksu and samgyetang. ☎ +82-2-778-1988

name: Ttosuni Sundae (또순이원조순대)
notes: VisitKorea: started as a street stand in 1976 and became the biggest sundae (blood sausage) restaurant in Sundae Town. White sundae, sundae guk, and sundae gopchang bokkeum. Sillim-dong is south of the centre (near Sillim Station) — a destination stop, not a Myeongdong walk. ☎ +82-2-884-7565

name: OPPADAK Myeongdong (오븐에빠진닭 명동)
address: 1F, Myeongdong Art Nouveau Centum, 21 Myeongdong 7-gil, Jung-gu (Myeongdong)
notes: VisitKorea: baked (oven-roasted) chicken — the house dish is crispy baked chicken. OPPADAK is a chain; this page is the Myeongdong branch only, so these hours are for this shop. One of the few Myeongdong options open past midnight. ☎ +82-2-3789-5892

name: Insadong Garlic Bossam (인사동마늘보쌈)
notes: VisitKorea: maneul bossam (pork wraps with garlic), kimchijjim, nakji bokkeum, buchujeon and ttukbaegi dubu kimchi, also as a set menu; the page says free makgeolli on weekdays 11:00–14:00. No parking. ☎ +82-2-735-7885 · insadonggarlicbossam.com

name: Gomgukshijip Myeongdong Branch (곰국시집 명동)
notes: VisitKorea: open since 1976; guksu jeongol (noodle hot pot) and gomkuksi (beef-bone noodle soup), plus mandu jeongol and grilled hanu / Wagyu. Between Myeongdong and Euljiro 1-ga stations. ☎ +82-2-756-3449

name: Hanttukbaegi (한뚝배기)
notes: VisitKorea: a Korean restaurant in Seomyeon where you can order for one; boiled pork slices (suyuk) is the famous menu, bulgogi hot pot the other. ☎ +82-51-807-0955
hours: Open 24 hours. (No closing day printed on the listing.)

name: Daom (다옴)
notes: Visit Busan: casual Korean dining; chadolbagi bibimguksu (brisket mixed noodles), kalguksu and bibimbap are the signatures; broth from southern-coast anchovies and a fruit-aged marinade. ☎ +82-507-1370-3778
hours: Mon–Thu & Sun 11:00–22:00 (last order 21:00) / Fri–Sat 11:00–22:30 (last order 21:30). Open 365 days.

name: Sogonggan
notes: Visit Busan: 1++-rated Korean beef course restaurant; the name means both "small space" and skill at cooking beef. Fixed lunch and dinner courses (portal prices not copied). No Korean name printed on the page. ☎ 010-5191-9002

name: Woobong Shabu
notes: Visit Busan: premium shabu shabu with 1++-rated beef cooked in a paper pot. Cheongsapo is a coastal village east of Haeundae beach. No Korean name printed on the page. ☎ +82-507-1349-9256

name: bibibidang
notes: Visit Busan: traditional Korean teahouse using antique Goryeo celadon and Joseon white-porcelain teapots; matcha and pumpkin shaved ice are listed. No Korean name printed on the page. ☎ 051-746-0705

name: Seoul Samgyetang (서울삼계탕)
notes: VisitKorea (halal-friendly listing): samgyetang, red-ginseng samgyetang and rotisserie chicken. Marked pork-free; no prayer room. Despite the "Seoul" name this is a Nampo, Busan restaurant — not the same shop as Nampo Samgyetang (남포삼계탕) at 16 Nampo-gil. ☎ +82-51-245-3696

name: Gwangangukbap (광안국밥)
notes: Visit Busan: dwaeji gukbap in front of Gwangalli Beach, known for thick broth and soft meat; also spicy soup and rice, steamed pork and sundae jeongol. ☎ +82-51-757-0720

name: Subok Dwaejigukbap (수복돼지국밥)
notes: Visit Busan: dwaeji gukbap and suyuk baekban; sundae, kimchi and kkakdugi made in-house; parking available. ☎ 051-866-3349

name: Tongyoung oyster&octopus love (통영굴사랑&낙지사랑)
notes: VisitKorea (halal-friendly listing): Tongyeong oyster rice and stir-fried octopus with rice; halal menu and pork-free, but no prayer room. 40 seats. VisitKorea prints the street as "Haenggung-rom" (a typo for Haenggung-ro). ☎ +82-31-252-1253
hours: 10:00–21:00. (No closing day printed on the listing.)

name: Suhyang Bapsang (수향밥상)
notes: Visit Busan: loach specialty restaurant popular with families; the rich loach soup (chueotang) is the signature, with short rib soup the other listed order. The portal notes the owners run their own fish farm to control the ingredients. Far west of the city in Dadae-dong — a destination, not a walk-in. ☎ 051-266-4726

name: Samnak Hadong Jaecheopguk
notes: Visit Busan: freshwater clam soup (jaecheopguk) house in the Samnak clam-soup cluster; the portal says they use only domestic Seomjingang River clams, soaked in salt water and washed several times before boiling, and that they also developed raw and steamed clam dishes. The listing adds a one-off note: closed on Lunar New Year's Day (17 Feb) 2026. The official English page prints no Korean name, so search the address on Naver Map rather than a transliteration. ☎ 051-301-7200

name: Bubu Coffee
notes: Visit Busan: small cafe run by a couple, roasting their own dark-roast specialty coffee. In Gwangbok-dong, walking distance from Jagalchi and BIFF Square — a useful daytime stop on the Nampo-dong loop. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ 010-7516-0484

name: Donghwa Banjeom
notes: Visit Busan: billed as the first Chinese restaurant in Busan, founded 1950, moved to Bosu-dong in 1987. Signatures are yuni jjajang and nanjawanseu (Korean-Chinese meatballs). The portal notes the group also has a store in Namcheon-dong, Nam-gu — **this entry is the Bosu-dong (Jung-gu) address only**. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-51-253-6661

name: Myeonok Hyangcheon
notes: Visit Busan: buckwheat noodle house at the entrance to the traditional market in U-dong, grinding its own flour on millstones and a mill; morisoba and makguksu can be ordered at 100% buckwheat. House-made sauces, and the portal singles out the croquettes served on the side. Lunch only. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-51-747-4601

name: Jinmi Eonyang Bulgogi
notes: Visit Busan: Eonyang-style bulgogi (the Ulsan style of hand-chopped beef) grilled for you by the staff, with a stew served after the meat. The portal frames it as a favourite of singer Sung Si-kyung and says it featured on his YouTube channel — that is the portal's claim, not independently checked here. 6-minute walk from Geumnyeonsan Station Exit 1 (Line 2). **Not the same restaurant as Gwangalli Eonyang Bulgogi Busanjip** also in this guide: different street number (7 Namcheonbada-ro 33beon-gil vs 32 Namcheonbada-ro) and different phone. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-51-753-1632

name: Pro Soy Crab (Main Branch)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 2 Jun 2026): opened 1980 and widely called Korea's foremost ganjang-gejang house. Soy-marinated crab, spicy marinated crab, braised blue crab and sannakji. The listing notes a second location in Samseong-dong — **this entry is the Sinsa main branch only**. Sinsa Station (Line 3 / Sinbundang) Exit 4, 153m. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-2-543-4126 · prosoycrab.co.kr

name: Busanjib KBBQ
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 30 Jun 2026): halal Korean barbecue in the middle of Myeongdong — hanwoo sirloin, wagyu rib fingers and lamb ribs with Korean banchan. No alcohol sold; Muslim cooks on staff. Same operator as Myeongdong Busanjib and Busanjib Fried Chicken, but a separate address and a separate listing — **this entry is 11-8 only**. ☎ +82-10-3142-0278

name: Busanjib Fried Chicken
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 30 Jun 2026): Korean fried chicken made with halal ingredients — plain fried, plus a fiercely spicy seasoned version. No alcohol sold; Muslim cooks on staff. Same operator as Myeongdong Busanjib and Busanjib KBBQ; **this entry is 11-4 only**. ☎ +82-10-3142-0278

name: Byeolnan Ori (별난오리)
notes: VisitKorea (halal-friendly listing): duck specialist near Dongdaemun — grilled smoked duck, duck soup (byeolnan oritang) and a duck set. Pork-free; **no prayer room**. 70 seats, 3 parking spaces. ☎ +82-2-765-5292

name: Daehan Gopchang (Jangan Branch)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 28 May 2025): grilled beef intestines — gopchang, makchang and daechang, with the all-in-one set the house recommendation, finished with fried rice. The portal warns that since the restaurant appeared on "I Live Alone" it often sells out and closes early, so go early rather than late despite the 01:00 posted close. Janghanpyeong Station (Line 5) Exit 3, 193m. Branch page — **this Jangan branch only**. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-70-8285-6219
hours: Daily 15:00–01:00 (next day). Note: the listing itself warns they often sell out and close early.

name: Seongcheon Makguksu (성천막국수)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 3 Jun 2026): makguksu — cold buckwheat noodles in a pure dongchimi broth, high buckwheat content. The set with jeyuk (spicy marinated pork) and dongchimi radish is the house order. **Caution: the official page contradicts itself on Saturday.** It prints "Mon - Sat 11:30 - 15:00 / 17:00 - 21:00" and then "Sat 11:30 - 17:00, including holidays: 11:30 AM – 3:00 PM" — both lines are reproduced here as printed; ring ahead if you are going on a Saturday. Dapsimni Station (Line 5) Exit 4, 764m. ☎ +82-507-1329-5529
hours: Mon–Sat 11:30–15:00 / 17:00–21:00; the same page also prints "Sat 11:30–17:00, including holidays 11:30–15:00". Closed Sundays, Seollal & Chuseok.

name: Cheongdamgol
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 4 Jun 2026): a plain baekban house in expensive Cheongdam, known for nurungji baekban (scorched-rice set) served with kimchi jjigae and ten-plus side dishes including steamed egg, soy-marinated crab and seasoned vegetables. Gangnam-gu Office Station (Line 7 / Suin-Bundang) Exit 4, 797m. Hours as read from the official page on 19 Aug 2026. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-2-543-1252

name: Yangmani (Cheongdam Branch)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 4 Jun 2026): grilled ox tripe (yang) and large intestine in a clean, comfortable room — New Zealand tripe, Korean large intestine — plus yangwutang, tripe simmered with dried cabbage. Open around the clock. Branch page: **this Cheongdam branch only**; the Yeouido branch is listed separately in this guide with different hours. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-2-542-9263

name: Yangmani (Yeouido)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 18 Aug 2026): tripe marinated 24 hours in a house sauce and grilled, plus other cuts. A different venue from the Cheongdam branch also in this guide — different address, different phone and different hours; the two were cross-checked before both were kept. National Assembly Station (Line 9) Exit 2, 435m. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-507-1421-9282
hours: Daily 10:30–22:00, with a Mon–Fri break 14:30–16:30. Closed Seollal & Chuseok.

name: Yi Ning
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 26 Jun 2026): Sichuan and Cantonese cooking in a spare black interior; the steamed rockfish with coriander, ginger and shredded spring onion is the popular order, with gajisaeu (shrimp with aubergine) and balchaejjim (steamed fat choy) as the less usual ones. Peking duck is listed as the signature dish. Long-running by Cheongdam standards. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-2-547-7444

name: MAO
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 26 Jun 2026): one of the few Peking duck specialists in Seoul, with a broad Cantonese menu alongside. Directly opposite Yangmani's Cheongdam branch. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-2-514-8803

name: Moodeungsan
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 4 Jun 2026): charcoal-grilled beef, rib eye above all, with a long banchan spread and naengmyeon to finish. Accessible pathways marked on the listing. Runs late — midnight on weekdays. Not to be confused with the Myeongdong restaurant of a similar name, which is **not** in this guide. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-507-1409-4017 · moodeungsan.com

name: Haemok Nonhyeon
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 30 Jun 2026): hitsumabushi — Japanese-style grilled eel over rice, lightly seasoned, in a room built to feel like Japan. Alcohol sold; no Muslim cooks. Gangnam-gu Office Station (Line 7 / Suin-Bundang) Exit 3-1, 600m. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-507-1466-0277

name: Onion (Seongsu)
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 13 May 2026): the original Seongsu branch of Cafe Onion, in a converted 1970s parts factory with the industrial fabric left exposed. Over twenty breads, with Pandoro and Ang Butter named as the signatures. Seongsu Station (Line 2) Exit 2, 132m. Branch page — **this Seongsu location only**. Open on holidays. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-507-1386-3238 · onionkr.com
hours: Mon–Fri 08:00–22:00 / weekends 09:00–22:00 (last order 21:30). Open daily, including holidays.

name: Kervan Cafe (케르반 카페)
notes: VisitKorea (halal-friendly listing): Turkish cafe and bakery just off the Usadan-ro slope below Seoul Central Mosque. Turkish apple tea and Turkish coffee are the listed orders. Halal menu, alcohol-free, pork-free, Muslim chef, and a prayer room is available. 30 seats, no parking. ☎ +82-70-7532-1997 · turkishbakery.co.kr

name: Samarkandcity (사마르칸트시티)
notes: VisitKorea (halal-friendly listing): Uzbek restaurant near Dongdaemun History & Culture Park, in the Central Asian pocket off Eulji-ro. Lamb chop set and shashlik set are the listed orders. Halal menu and pork-free, and a prayer room is available. 80 seats, no parking. Opens at 09:00 at weekends — unusually early for the area. ☎ +82-2-6014-6368

name: Mugyo-dong Bugeo-guk
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 2 Jun 2026): bugeo-guk — dried pollack soup — since 1968, made with firmly dried pollack rather than the frozen fish the portal says many rivals use. Opens at 07:00, which makes it one of the few proper breakfasts in the centre; queues at lunch. Note the listing also still carries a stale one-off banner, "Temporary Closure Due to the June 3 Local Elections" — that date has passed and it is not a standing closure. City Hall Station (Lines 1/2) Exit 4, 322m. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-2-777-3891
hours: Weekdays 07:00–20:00 / weekends & holidays 07:00–15:00. Closed Lunar New Year & Chuseok.

name: Jihwaja
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 2 Jun 2026): royal-court cuisine house running since 1991 under a holder of the Korean royal cuisine tradition; degustation courses and set menus (grilled beef ribs, braised short ribs, soy-braised abalone, seafood hot pot), cooked without MSG or artificial flavourings. Booking essentially required. **Read the closing days with care:** the page's Days of Operation field says Wednesday–Sunday, and its holiday field says "closed every Monday and Tuesday" but qualifies it "(Through July 31)" and lists a summer break of 6–11 July — both dated qualifiers have already passed, so confirm the current closing days when you book. ☎ +82-2-2269-5834 · jihwajafood.co.kr
hours: 11:30–15:00 / 17:00–21:30 (last order 18:30). Days of Operation printed as Wed–Sun, i.e. closed Mondays and Tuesdays — but see the dated qualifier in the notes.

name: Mongmyeok Sanbang
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 4 Jun 2026): a short menu of plainly presented Korean dishes in a hanok on the Namsan slope — bibimbap, buchu jeon, dotori muk and house-made traditional teas. 433m from Myeongdong Station Exit 2, so it is the closest thing to a quiet lunch within walking distance of the Myeongdong crowds. Minor wrinkle on the official page: the Days of Operation field reads Monday–Sunday while the holiday field says closed Tuesdays — the closing day is recorded here as Tuesday. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-2-318-4790

name: Eulji Dabang
notes: Visit Seoul (edited 1 Aug 2026): a 1985 dabang — an old-style Korean tea room — kept intact on a second floor among the Euljiro towers. The listed orders are ssanghwa tea served with a raw egg yolk floating in it like a full moon, plus ramen, cold coffee, plum tea and schisandra juice. Opens at 06:00 on weekdays, which makes it an unusually early stop. Euljiro 3-ga Station (Lines 2/3) Exit 10, 30m. The official English page prints no Korean name. ☎ +82-2-2272-1886
hours: Mon–Sat 06:00–21:00 / Sun 09:00–20:00. No closing days printed.

hours: Weekdays 11:30–15:00 / 17:00–22:00; weekends 11:30–22:00. Closed Lunar New Year & Chuseok.

name: Noneun Bada (노는바다)

hours: Mon–Thu 17:00–24:00 / Fri–Sat 17:00–01:00. Closed Sundays and 1 January.

name: Kyoto Donburi Main Branch (교토돈부리본점)

hours: Weekdays 11:00–16:00 / 17:00–22:00; weekends 11:00–22:00. Closed on public holidays.
